title: Nonstandard-kernel-fallback-benchplan
content:
Summary:
This doc defines a reproducible benchmark and instrumentation harness to measure functional and performance impacts when requests traverse heterogeneous kernel stacks (TensorRT, Triton-backed CPU/GPU, and custom operator libraries) and when automatic fallback or routing occurs. The focus is on two problem classes: 1) silent numerical drift / output divergence after fallback, and 2) latency and tail-behavior changes when KV cache and kernel affinity must be migrated.

Motivation / Why now:
- We frequently push experimental custom kernels and see occasional production incidents where fallback to a Triton/Torch implementation changes answers in subtle ways.
- Customers expect consistent outputs when pinning model versions; our fallback and routing policies must not introduce surprising regressions.
- We need a minimal, repeatable harness that captures token-level deltas, per-request latency distributions, memory pressure events, and KV cache integrity checks across kernel transitions.

Hypotheses to test:
1) Mixed-precision custom kernels (FP16/INT8) with different fusion strategies will cause <0.1% top-token delta vs baseline on most workloads but higher divergence on long-context summarization prompts.
2) KV cache migration during fallback produces a measurable latency spike (p50->p95 delta) proportional to active KV size; final throughput impact depends on whether migration is synchronous or opportunistic.
3) Determinism mismatches (RNG, layernorm epsilon differences, kernel reorderings) are the primary source of functional drift rather than quantization noise alone.

Experiment matrix (plan):
- Axis A (kernel stacks): TensorRT (TRT) 23.x optimized; Triton v2-wrap CPU fallback; Custom fused-kernel lib v0.9; Reference PyTorch baseline (no fusion).
- Axis B (precision/config): FP16, INT8 (calibrated), FP32 baseline.
- Axis C (workloads): short-chat (<=256 tokens), long-context summarization (~4k tokens), streaming partial-completion load, multi-turn chat with KV re-use.
- Axis D (fallback modes): immediate-synchronous fallback, async-shadow-mirror then switch, per-token kernel selection (hybrid).
- Axis E (KV states): cold start (no cache), warm cache (single-user continuity), hot-large (KV size tuned to 75% GPU memory).

For each combination run: 1) functional correctness checks 2) latency percentiles (p50,p90,p99) 3) throughput (tokens/sec) 4) memory high-water mark and OOM incidence 5) time-to-fallback and migration duration 6) token-level divergence metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/normalized-l2/delta-top1).

Test harness design and implementation notes:
- Single-run harness executable (bench-runner) that can deploy controlled requests against an instrumented serving instance. Use a docker-compose topology for local runs and a k8s job for cluster scale.
- Instrumentation hooks: kernel-entry/exit times, per-kernel-op perf counters, KV-cache read/write telemetry (hit/miss, bytes moved), and deterministic seed control exposed to runtime.
- Determinism control: force global RNG seeds, unify layernorm eps across kernels by providing compatibility override, and disable non-deterministic cuDNN heuristics where possible.
- Shadowing: implement an optional shadow path that executes fallback kernel in parallel and computes token-level diffs without affecting live responses. Useful to collect divergence statistics in production-like loads.
- Migration strategies: synchronous full KV copy, incremental page-swap (opportunistic), and logical mapping (repointing pointers without copy) depending on compatibility. Each is instrumented and timed.

Workloads & datasets:
- Synthetic: parametrized tokens with repeated patterns to stress KV reuse (e.g., long prompt with repeated context prefix).
- Realistic: internal customer workloads anonymized (support chat transcripts, doc-summarization batches).
- Evaluation prompts: 200 random prompts per workload size bucket; for long-context run specialized summaries and chain-of-thought style sequences to expose numerical brittleness.

Metrics definitions and thresholds:
- Functional delta: normalized token agreement (fraction of tokens where top-1 matches baseline) and normalized-l2 on logits. Alert if token agreement < 99.9% for short-chat or < 99.5% for long-context.
- Latency SLO impact: acceptable increase p95 <= +15ms absolute for dedicated hardware; flag if +30ms.
- Migration disruption: time-to-stable throughput after a fallback <= 2s for opportunistic strategies; synchronous full KV copy should complete < 500ms for KV size <= 50MB.
- Memory safety: zero silent OOMs; any OOM must produce deterministic, logged error and cause rollback.

Data collection and analysis plan:
- Store full trace logs for a sample of requests (1 in 1000) including op-level timestamps, kernel identifiers, RNG seeds, and pre/post logits.
- Aggregate daily dashboards: divergence heatmap by model-layer, fallback-rate by route, and percentiles for fallback-induced latency.
- Post-run artifact: canonical run bundle (bench-runner config, kernel builds hashes, raw traces, summary csv). Archives uploaded to S3 with naming: kernel-bench/YYYYMMDD/{matrix-hash}.tar.gz

Runbook for anomalies (what to do when divergence observed):
1) Capture canonical request and seeds from trace.
2) Re-run single-request in deterministic mode across all kernels to reproduce.
3) If divergence reproducible, bisect by disabling fusions/quant steps to isolate operator causing non-determinism.
4) If divergence only on warm KV, examine KV serialization formats and pointer mapping during migration.
5) Create Jira (INF-xxxx) with reproducer attached; label as "customer-impacting" if match found in prod traces.

Instrumentation checklist (to be implemented in runtime before bench runs):
- Unique kernel IDs emitted per op (kernel.author/version).
- Per-op checksum of input tensor shapes and a lightweight hash of data for cheap divergence detection.
- KV-cache operation counters exposed via Prometheus (read/write/copy/fallback-swaps).
- Fallback event counter with reason codes (OOM, kernel-error, healthcheck, manual-route).

Patch / build requirements:
- Container images for: baseline-pytorch, triton-serve, tensorrt-optimized runtime, custom-kernel-debug build.
- Kernel builds must include a "compatibility shim" exposing layernorm_eps and RNG override flags.

Timeline and owners:
- Week 1: implement bench-runner + basic instrumentation (Eleanor + Marcus).
- Week 2: kernel builds and deterministic-mode flags (Dmitri + Ravi).
- Week 3: short-chat and KV-cold experiments; collect initial divergence matrix (All).
- Week 4: long-context stress and migration strategy runs; triage runs and update rollback policies (All).

Deliverables:
- Bench-runner repo branch with reproducible configs.
- A results dashboard prototype and raw dataset for initial 24 experiments.
- A short playbook (one-pager) for SREs describing how to detect and mitigate kernel-fallback regressions in production.

Open questions / risks:
- Calibration data for INT8: do we calibrate once per-model artifact or per-deployment? Calibration drift could mask or exacerbate divergence.
- Shadowing cost: running parallel kernels doubles compute; we need sampling heuristics to limit overhead.
- Non-deterministic GPU kernels that cannot be fully controlled via flags will limit our ability to ascribe divergence causes.

Notes & quick links:
- Example reproducer folder: s3://redwood-internal/kernel-bench/reproducers/20250109/
- GH prototype for shadow-runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/feature/shadow-runner
- Related Jira: INF-5421 (kernel fallback telemetry)

Next steps (short):
- Review plan with runtime maintainers and SRE (this week).
- Land minimal bench-runner with token-level diffing by end of Week 1.
- Schedule pilot runs on a dedicated cluster with isolated GPUs and controlled KV sizes.

Appendix (quick commands):
- Run local: ./bench-runner --config experiments/nonstandard-fallback.yaml --replay-seed 42 --collect-traces 100
- Upload artifacts: ./bench-runner --bundle results/20250112/ --upload s3://redwood-internal/kernel-bench/
